Rashi on Gittin 21b:10:1.hebrew: אין כותבין במחובר - דכתיב "וכתב ונתן", שאינו מחוסר קציצה:
Rashi on Gittin 21b:10:1.english: One may not write on [something] attached - for it is written, "And he writes ... and gives," [meaning something] that does not lack cutting [from the ground]:

Rashi on Gittin 21b:10:2.hebrew: כתב על המחובר כו' - בגמ' פריך: הא אמרת "אין כותבין":
Rashi on Gittin 21b:10:2.english: [If] one wrote [it] on what is attached, etc. - In the Gemara it asks: Didn't you say, "One may not write"?

Rashi on Gittin 21b:11:1.hebrew: נייר המחוק - יכול לחזור ולמוחקו עד העדים ולכותבו, ויעביר תנאי שהיה בו, ולא מוכחא מילתא, דהא עדים נמי על המחק חתומים. וכן דיפתרא — אין מחק שלו ניכר; ובגמ' מפרש מאי דיפתרא:
Rashi on Gittin 21b:11:1.english: Erased paper - One can go back and erase it up to [the signatures of] the witnesses and rewrite it, and [thereby] remove a condition that was in it, and the matter is not apparent, since the witnesses too are signed on the erasure. And similarly [with] diftera — its erasure is not noticeable; and in the Gemara it explains what diftera is:

Rashi on Gittin 21b:11:2.english: And the Sages deem [it] valid - [this] is explained in the Gemara:

Rashi on Gittin 21b:12:1.hebrew: והוא ששייר - סיפא דקתני כשר, והוא ששייר מקום התורף וכתבו לאחר תלישה:
Rashi on Gittin 21b:12:1.english: Provided that he left - [Regarding] the latter clause [of the Mishnah], which teaches [that it is] valid: [this applies] provided that he left the place of the toref [the essential part of the document] and wrote it after detachment:

Rashi on Gittin 21b:12:2.hebrew: תורף - גלויו של שטר, מקום האיש והאשה והזמן:
Rashi on Gittin 21b:12:2.english: Toref [the essential part] - The exposed [essential] part of a document, [namely] the place [for the names] of the man, the woman, and the date:

Rashi on Gittin 21b:13:1.hebrew: ור' אלעזר היא - מתני' דבעי כתיבה בתלוש, דדריש "וכתב" דקרא אכתב הגט ולא אחתימת עדים, רבי אלעזר היא, דאמר: חתימת הגט אינה מן התורה, אלא מפני תיקון העולם; הילכך, "וכתב" דקרא אכתב הגט קאי:
Rashi on Gittin 21b:13:1.english: And it is Rabbi Elazar - [The] Mishnah, which requires writing on [something] detached [from the ground] — as it expounds "and he writes" of the verse [as referring] to the writing of the bill of divorce and not to the signing of the witnesses — is [in accordance with] Rabbi Elazar, who says [that] the signing of the bill of divorce is not by Torah law, but rather for the betterment of the world; therefore, "and he writes" of the verse refers to the writing of the bill of divorce:

Rashi on Gittin 21b:15:1.hebrew: חתמו שנינו - בסיפא דמתני': "תלשו, חתמו, ונתנו לה, כשר", ואע"פ שנכתב כולו במחובר, דכי כתיב "וכתב" דקרא, אחתימת עדים שהיא עיקר, ור' מאיר היא:
Rashi on Gittin 21b:15:1.english: We learned "they signed it" - in the latter clause of the Mishnah: "[If] he detached it, they signed it, and he gave it to her, it is valid," even though all of it was written while attached [to the ground]; for when "and he writes" of the verse is written, [it refers] to the signature of the witnesses, which is the essential [part], and it is [the view of] Rabbi Meir:

Rashi on Gittin 21b:17:1.hebrew: דשקיל ליה - לכוליה עציץ, ואין כאן מחוסר קציצה; ואין לחוש שמא ישבר החרס ויתן לה החתיכה והויא ליה קציצה, דלא מפסיד ליה לעציץ:
Rashi on Gittin 21b:17:1.english: As he takes it - [He takes] the entire pot, so there is no [issue of] lacking detachment here; and there is no concern lest he break the earthenware and give her the piece, [such that] it would constitute detachment, since he would not ruin the pot:

Rashi on Gittin 21b:1:1.hebrew: לא אפשר למקצייה - דשייך העבד במצות, ואינו רשאי לחבל בו; ואם חבל בו — יוצא לחירות בראשי אברים, אלמא אינו רשאי לחבל בו:
Rashi on Gittin 21b:1:1.english: It is not possible to cut it off - Because [the slave] is obligated in mitzvot, and [the master] is not permitted to injure him; and if he did injure him, [the slave] goes free for [the loss of] major limbs — thus [we see] that he is not permitted to injure him:

Rashi on Gittin 21b:3:2.hebrew: וכתב לה מכל מקום - מדלא כתב "ונתן ספר כריתות בידה":
Rashi on Gittin 21b:3:2.english: And he writes her, in any case - Since [the verse] did not write, "and he places a scroll of severance in her hand":

Rashi on Gittin 21b:4:1.hebrew: אי כתב בספר - משמע יכתוב בקלף, ומצית למימר דכי רבי מ"וכתב לה", דומיא דקלף הוא דרבי:
Rashi on Gittin 21b:4:1.english: If it were written "besefer" [in a scroll] - it would imply "he shall write on parchment," and you could say that when [the Torah] includes [other surfaces] from [the words] "and he shall write for her," it is [only things] similar to parchment that it includes:

Rashi on Gittin 21b:4:2.hebrew: השתא דכתיב ספר - אין זו אלא "וכתב" ספירת דברי כריתות, ועל כל מה דבעי לכתוב:
Rashi on Gittin 21b:4:2.english: Now that it is written: “Scroll [sefer]” - this [means] nothing other than “and he shall write” an account of words of severance, and [it may be written] on whatever [surface] he wishes to write [it]:

Rashi on Gittin 21b:5:1.hebrew: וכתב לה מאי עבדי ליה - לדידהו לא איצטריך לרבות כל דבר, שהרי לא קבע הכתוב דבר לכתיבתו, ומונתן ספר כריתות שמעינן:
Rashi on Gittin 21b:5:1.english: “And he writes [for] her” — what do they do with it - For them, it is not needed to include every [writing] material, for Scripture did not specify any material for its writing, and we learn [this] from “and he gives [her] a scroll of severance”:

Rashi on Gittin 21b:5:2.hebrew: ואינה מתגרשת בכסף - אם אמר לה, "הילך פרוטה והתגרשי לי בה":
Rashi on Gittin 21b:5:2.english: And she is not divorced with money - [That is,] if he said to her, "Here is a perutah for you, and be divorced to me with it":

Rashi on Gittin 21b:5:3.hebrew: אקיש יציאה להוייה - כדכתיב "ויצאה והיתה לאיש אחר":
Rashi on Gittin 21b:5:3.english: I should juxtapose leaving [marriage] to becoming [married] - As it is written: "and she leaves and becomes [married] to another man":

Rashi on Gittin 21b:5:4.hebrew: הוייה - קידושין, שמהוה בהן עצמה לבעל:
Rashi on Gittin 21b:5:4.english: Becoming [married] - Betrothal, through which she becomes [a wife] to a husband:

Rashi on Gittin 21b:6:1.english: From "scroll of severance" - Since [Scripture] juxtaposed "severance" to "scroll":

Rashi on Gittin 21b:7:1.hebrew: דבר הכורת - שלא יהא בו תנאי המקשרן יחד, אלא תנאי הכורת ומבדיל ביניהם:
Rashi on Gittin 21b:7:1.english: A matter that severs - [meaning] that there should not be in it [the bill of divorce] a condition that binds them together, but rather a condition that severs and separates between them:

Rashi on Gittin 21b:7:2.english: [If he says,] "Forever," that is not severance - for all her days she is bound to him:

Rashi on Gittin 21b:8:1.english: From karet, keritut - for [the verse] could have written sefer karet:

Tosafot on Gittin 21b:2:1.hebrew: יצא זה שמחוסר כתיבה קציצה כו' - פי' רבינו שמואל דוקא בבעלי חיים או במחובר לקרקע שעוקר דבר מגידולו חשיב מחוסר קציצה. ותדע, דבסמוך איפליגו אביי ורבא כשכתבו על עלה של עציץ נקוב, דרבא גזר שמא יקטום, אבל כשאינו נקוב משמע אפי' יקטום כשר; וכן פירש הרב רבי שמעיה בפירושו. ואם כתב גט בקלף גדול ואח"כ חתכו, לפי זה כשר. ומעשה היה בימי ה"ר יצחק ברבי מנחם, ופסלו, ונחלקו עליו גדולי הדור. ובה"ג פוסל, וכן ר"ת היה מחמיר, מדקאמר בסמוך: כתבו על חרס של עציץ נקוב כשר, דשקיל ליה ויהיב לה ניהליה; והא דלא פליג עלה רבא, משום דליכא למיגזר שמא ישבר העציץ, דאין דרך לשוברו, כמו בקרן של פרה דלא גזרי' שמא יקצץ, דאין דרך ליקצץ, ודוקא בעלה גזרי' שמא יקטום. ולאו דוקא נקט עלה של עציץ נקוב, דהוא הדין כשאינו נקוב, אלא משום רבותא דאביי נקטיה, דאפילו בנקוב מכשיר. ועוד אור"י, דמסתבר דאין האשה קונה את הגט שכתוב על עלה של עציץ נקוב במשיכת העציץ או בהגבהתו, כל זמן שלא פסקה יניקת העלה, כדאמרינן בסמוך: מכר בעל זרעים לבעל עציץ, לא קנה עד שיחזיק בזרעים, אבל במשיכת העציץ לא קנה, דאכתי חשיבי מחוברין בשעת משיכה; והא דמכשיר אביי משום דשקיל ליה ויהיב לה, היינו דהניחתו במקום שפוסקת יניקת העציץ, דהשתא הוי רבותא טפי דמכשיר אביי בעציץ נקוב, דלא גזרי' דיהיב לה בפסיקת היניקה אטו בלא פסיקת היניקה; וקמ"ל נמי אע"פ שצריך ליתן לה בפסיקת היניקה, לא חשיב בהכי מחוסר קציצה. ור"י מייתי ראיה לפי' ר"ת, דחשיב בפ' כסוי הדם (חולין דף פט.) עפר עיר הנדחת מחוסר תלישה, קביצה ושריפה, ויותר נחשב מחובר גט בקלף גדול מחיבור עפר עיר הנדחת. והא דלא חשיב לקורה הנעוצה בארץ מחוסר תלישה בפ' נגמר הדין (סנהדרין דף מו:), משום דלא חשיב חיבור לקרקע כולי האי. ולר"ת, דוקא נחתך מקלף גדול חשיב מחוסר קציצה, אבל חותך מן הגט דבר מועט כמו שעושין לייפותו, לא חשיב בהכי מחוסר קציצה, כדאמרי' לעיל: גזייה לזמן ויהבי' ניהלה כו', בין שיטה לשיטה בין תיבה לתיבה מהו, גבי "והנייר שלי", משמע דדבר מועט לא חשיב מחוסר קציצה:
Tosafot on Gittin 21b:2:1.english: Excluding this, which is lacking writing, cutting, etc. - Rabbeinu Shmuel explained [that] specifically with living creatures or with something attached to the ground, where one detaches a thing from its growth, is it considered lacking cutting. And you should know [this], for shortly below Abaye and Rava disagree when one wrote [a get] on a leaf of a perforated pot: Rava decrees [it invalid] lest he pluck [the leaf], whereas when it is unperforated, it implies [that] even if he plucks [it], it is valid; and so too Rabbi Shemayah explained in his commentary. And if he wrote a get on a large parchment and afterwards cut it [off], according to this [view] it is valid. And an incident occurred in the days of HaRav Rabbi Yitzchak ben Rabbi Menachem, and he ruled it invalid, and the great scholars of the generation disagreed with him. And the Ba'al Halakhot Gedolot rules [it] invalid, and so too Rabbeinu Tam was stringent, based on what [the Gemara] says shortly below: "If he wrote it on the shard of a perforated pot, it is valid, for he takes it and gives it to her"; and the reason Rava does not disagree with this is because there is no [reason] to decree [it invalid] lest the pot be broken, since it is not normal to break it — just like with the horn of a cow, where we do not decree [it invalid] lest it be cut off, since it is not normal to cut [it] off, and only with a leaf do we decree lest he pluck [it]. And it was not specifically [that] it mentioned a leaf of a perforated pot, for the same law applies when it is unperforated; rather, because of the novelty of Abaye['s ruling] it mentioned it, that even in [the case of] a perforated [pot] he rules [it] valid. Furthermore, Ri says that it is reasonable that the woman does not acquire the get that is written on a leaf of a perforated pot through pulling the pot or through lifting it, as long as the nourishment of the leaf has not ceased, as we say shortly below: "If the owner of the seeds sold [them] to the owner of the pot, he has not acquired [them] until he takes possession of the seeds, but through pulling the pot he has not acquired [them]," because they are still considered attached at the time of pulling; and that which Abaye rules [it] valid because "he takes it and gives it to her" — that is when she placed it in a place where the nourishment of the pot ceases, for now it is a greater novelty that Abaye rules [it] valid with a perforated pot, since we do not decree [against] his giving [it] to her when the nourishment has ceased on account of [a case] without the nourishment having ceased; and [the Gemara] also teaches us [that] even though he must give [it] to her when the nourishment has ceased, it is not thereby considered lacking cutting. And Ri brings a proof for Rabbeinu Tam's explanation, for in the chapter [entitled] Kisui HaDam (Chullin 89a) [the Gemara] considers the earth of an idolatrous city [to be] lacking plucking, gathering, and burning; and a get on a large parchment is considered more attached than the attachment of the earth of an idolatrous city. And the reason [the Gemara] does not consider a beam stuck into the ground [to be] lacking plucking in the chapter [entitled] Nigmar HaDin (Sanhedrin 46b) is because it is not considered attached to the ground to that extent. And according to Rabbeinu Tam, specifically [when] it is cut from a large parchment is it considered lacking cutting; but [if] one cuts a small amount from the get, as they do to beautify it, it is not thereby considered lacking cutting, as we said above: "He cut off the date and gave it to her, etc."; "Between one line and the next, between one word and the next, what is [the law]?" regarding "and the paper is mine" — which implies that a small amount is not considered lacking cutting:

Tosafot on Gittin 21b:3:1.hebrew: תלמוד לומר וכתב לה מ"מ - וא"ת: ואימא "וכתב" כלל, "ספר" פרט, ואין בכלל אלא מה שבפרט? וי"ל: "ונתן" חזר וכלל, אע"ג דלא מייתי אלא כללא קמא. הכי נמי אשכחן בפ"ק דקידושין (דף כא:): "מרצע" — אין לי אלא מרצע, מנין לרבות הסול וכו'? ת"ל "ולקחת" — כל דבר הניקח ביד; ולא מייתי בברייתא כללא בתרא, ובסוגיא דהתם מוכח דכלל ופרט וכלל קא דריש, "ונתת באזנו" חזר וכלל:
Tosafot on Gittin 21b:3:1.english: The verse states: "And he writes her," in any case - And if you say: Let us say [that] "and he writes" is a generalization, "a scroll" is a specification, and a generalization [followed by a specification] includes only what is in the specification? One can answer: "And he gives" is a second generalization, even though [the baraita] only cites the first generalization. Similarly, we find in the first chapter of Kiddushin (21b): "'An awl' — I have [derived] only an awl; from where [do I derive] to include a thorn, etc.? The verse states: 'And you shall take' — anything that is taken in the hand"; and the baraita does not cite the final generalization, yet in the sugya there it is proven that it expounds [the verse as] a generalization, a specification, and a generalization, [as] "and you shall put [it] in his ear" is a second generalization:

Tosafot on Gittin 21b:3:2.hebrew: מה ספר דבר שאין בו רוח חיים - לא בעי למימר "מה ספר — דבר הבא מב"ח כו'", לאפוקי עלה וטבלא ופינקס, אף ע"ג דבפ"ק דקידושין (דף יז.) גבי הענקה אמרי' דאי כתיב "צאן", ה"א דוקא ב"ח אין, אבל גדולי קרקע לא; שמא לא חשיב כל כך צד חשוב דבר הבא מב"ח כמו צד של בעלי חיים עצמו. ועוד, דהכל כפי מה שדומה לחכמים נקיט בכל א' ענין הראוי לו; דבפ' בכל מערבין (עירובין דף כז:) נקט "פירי מפרי וגידולי קרקע", ובסוכה (דף יא:) "מה חגיגה — דבר שאינו מקבל טומאה [וגידולו מן הארץ] (ואינו אוכל)":
Tosafot on Gittin 21b:3:2.english: Just as a scroll is something that has no breath of life - [The Gemara] did not want to say, "Just as a scroll is something that comes from a living creature, etc.," [which would come] to exclude a leaf, a tablet, and a ledger, even though in the first chapter of Kiddushin (17a), regarding the severance gift [to a Hebrew slave], we say that if [only] "sheep" were written, I would have said that specifically living creatures — yes, but produce of the earth — no. Perhaps "something that comes from a living creature" is not considered such a significant aspect [for comparison] as the aspect of living creatures themselves. Furthermore, [it is] all according to what seems [fitting] to the Sages — they adopt in each [case] the formulation appropriate to it; for in the chapter [entitled] Bechol Me'arvin (Eruvin 27b) they used [the formulation] "fruit from fruit and produce of the earth," and in Sukkah (11b): "Just as the festival offering is something that is not susceptible to ritual impurity [and grows from the earth] (and is not food)":

Tosafot on Gittin 21b:5:1.hebrew: בכתיבה מתגרשת - תרי "וכתב לה" כתיב: אחד דרשינן "וכתב לה" — לשמה, ומ"וכתב" אחרינא — בכתיבה מתגרשת, ומ"לה" — לה ולא לה ולחברתה:
Tosafot on Gittin 21b:5:1.english: Via writing she is divorced - Two [instances of] "and he writes her" are written [in the Torah]: [from] one we expound "and he writes for her" — [that it must be written] for her sake; and from the other "and he writes" — [that] via writing she is divorced; and from "her" — for her, and not for her and her co-wife:

Tosafot on Gittin 21b:5:2.hebrew: ואינה מתגרשת בכסף - הך דרשה לרבא, אבל לאביי נפקא ליה דאינה מתגרשת בכסף מסברא, דיאמרו כסף מכניס כו'; ומ"מ איצטריך לדידיה נמי "וכתב" למעוטי חליצה. והתם ממעט חליצה מ"ספר כורתה" — היינו דרשה דר' יוסי הגלילי, ונקט לה לפי שהיא פשוטה, וכן רגיל בכמה דוכתי:
Tosafot on Gittin 21b:5:2.english: And she is not divorced via money - This exposition is according to Rava; but according to Abaye, he derives that she is not divorced via money from reasoning, [namely,] "They will say: money brings [her] in [so money should take her out]," etc. Nevertheless, for him too, "and he writes" is needed to exclude chalitzah. And there [where the Gemara] excludes chalitzah from "a document cuts her off" — that is the exposition of Rabbi Yosei HaGalili, and [the Gemara] cites it because it is straightforward, and so is it accustomed [to do] in several places:

Tosafot on Gittin 21b:7:1.hebrew: שלא תלכי לבית אביך לעולם אין זה כריתות - תימה: הא אם מת אביה או אם מכר, לא חשיב תו בית אביה, כדתנן בהשותפין (בנדרים דף מו.): "קונם לביתך שאיני נכנס, שדך שאיני לוקח — מת או מכר לאחר, מותר"! ויש לומר דכל יוצאי חלציו קרוים "בית אביו", ואפילו שמת, כדכתיב (בראשית לח): "שבי אלמנה בית אביך", גבי תמר, וכבר מת אביה, כדמוכחי קראי:
Tosafot on Gittin 21b:7:1.english: That you will not go to your father’s house forever, that is not severance - This is astonishing: if her father dies, or if he sold [the house], it is no longer considered "her father's house," as we learned in a Mishnah in [the chapter entitled] Hashutafin (Nedarim 46a): "[If one says to another,] 'Konam [that] I will not enter your house,' [or] '[that] I will not buy your field' — if he died or sold [it] to another, it is permitted!" And one can say that all of his descendants are called "his father's house," even when he has died, as it is written (Genesis 38[:11]): "Remain a widow [in] your father's house," regarding Tamar, and her father had already died, as the verses prove:

Tosafot on Gittin 21b:8:1.hebrew: ורבי יוסי הגלילי מכרת כריתות כו' - קשה לרבינו תם, דבפ' המגרש (לקמן גיטין פג:) קאמר על רבנן דרבי אלעזר בן עזריה ד"כרת כריתות" לא דרשי, ור' יוסי הגלילי הוא בכלל רבנן דהתם! ויש לומר דלא דרשי "כרת כריתות" לההיא דרשה דהתם, ולא בעי למימר דלא דרשי כלל:
Tosafot on Gittin 21b:8:1.english: And Rabbi Yosei HaGelili [derives it] from karet [and] keritut, etc. - [This] is difficult for Rabbeinu Tam: for in the chapter [entitled] HaMegaresh (below, Gittin 83b), [the Gemara] says regarding the Rabbis [who dispute] Rabbi Elazar ben Azariah that they do not expound [the difference between] karet [and] keritut, and Rabbi Yosei HaGelili is included among those Rabbis there! And one can say that they do not expound karet [and] keritut for that exposition there, and [the Gemara] does not mean to say that they do not expound [it] at all:
